seo.title: Plausible Alternative with Retention and User Profiles
seo.description: OpenPanel vs Plausible: both are cookieless and AGPL. OpenPanel adds retention, cohorts and user profiles. Prices at 10k to 10M pageviews, and when to stay put.

hero.heading: A Plausible alternative for when pageviews stop being enough
hero.subheading: Plausible tells you how many people came and where from. It can't tell you whether the people who signed up in March are still around in May, because it never knows who anyone is. OpenPanel keeps the cookieless web dashboard and adds retention, cohorts and user profiles on the same events.

competitor.name: Plausible Analytics
competitor.short_description: Cookieless web analytics with a one-page dashboard, hosted in Germany and built by a small bootstrapped team.

overview.title: What Plausible does well, and where it stops
paragraphs: Plausible is a well-made tool. The dashboard fits on one screen, the script is under 1 KB, and nobody on your team needs training to read it. If you run a blog, a docs site or a marketing site, it does the job and you can stop reading here.

The limit is by design. Plausible counts visitors anonymously and never ties events to a person, so it can't answer questions that need a person: what share of last month's signups came back this week, which accounts use a feature, what a single user did before they churned. Its funnels (2 to 8 steps) and user journeys exist, but only on the Business plan, and they count visitors within a visit rather than following a user over weeks.

OpenPanel tracks the same pageviews and referrers without cookies, then lets you call identify() when someone logs in. From that point the same events feed retention tables, cohorts you can reuse as filters, user profiles with their full event history, and funnels you can break down by any property. You don't need a second tool for the logged-in part of your product.

Self-hosting is the other difference. Plausible Community Edition ships twice a year and leaves out funnels, user journeys and revenue goals. OpenPanel's self-hosted version is the full product, with releases arriving a month or two after Cloud.

summary_comparison.title: OpenPanel vs Plausible: which one fits
summary_comparison.intro: Both are open source under AGPL-3.0, both are cookieless, and both host their cloud in Germany. The split is anonymous traffic stats versus product analytics on identified users.
summary_comparison.one_liner: Pick Plausible for traffic stats on a content site. Pick OpenPanel when you also need to know what logged-in users do over time.
best_for_openpanel: SaaS and apps that need retention by signup cohort
Teams that want funnels and user flows without paying for a Business tier
Products with logged-in users you need to look up one by one
Self-hosters who want funnels and retention, not a reduced community edition
Mobile apps: there are Swift, Kotlin and React Native SDKs
best_for_competitor: Blogs, docs and marketing sites that only need traffic numbers
Teams that want the smallest possible script (under 1 KB)
Anyone who needs to import years of Google Analytics history
People who value a dashboard nobody has to learn

competitor_strengths.title: Where Plausible is better
competitor_strengths.intro: For traffic stats on a content site, these are good reasons to stay.

items.title: A smaller script
items.description: Plausible's tracker is under 1 KB. OpenPanel's is about 3 KB gzipped. Both are small next to most analytics tools, but Plausible is smaller.

items.title: A dashboard nobody has to learn
items.description: Plausible puts everything for a site on one page. OpenPanel has more reports, which also means more to learn.

items.title: Google Analytics import
items.description: Plausible can import your Google Analytics history. OpenPanel can't, so a switch from GA starts with an empty chart.

items.title: Lower prices for traffic stats only
items.description: If you only need pageviews and sources, Plausible Starter is cheaper from 1M pageviews up: $69 against $90 at 1M, and $169 against $350 at 10M.

pricing.title: Pricing at the same traffic
pricing.intro: Plausible bills by monthly pageviews and puts funnels, user journeys and custom properties on Business. OpenPanel bills by events with every feature on every tier; one pageview is one event, and custom events count too. Plausible prices from plausible.io, October 18, 2026, monthly billing.

openpanel.model: Monthly event volume, all features included
openpanel.description: 10k events: $5. 100k: $20. 1M: $90. 10M: $350. 30-day free trial, then paid; there is no free tier. Self-hosting is free with no event limit.

competitor.description: Starter / Growth / Business at 10k pageviews: $9 / $14 / $19. 100k: $19 / $29 / $39. 1M: $69 / $104 / $139. 10M: $169 / $254 / $339. Yearly billing gives 2 months free. Funnels and user journeys need Business.

migration.title: Moving from Plausible to OpenPanel
migration.intro: There's no importer for Plausible data, so the usual path is to run both for a few weeks and switch once OpenPanel has enough history.
migration.estimated_time: An hour of setup, then a few weeks running both

steps.title: Add OpenPanel next to Plausible
steps.description: Install the script tag or SDK and leave Plausible running. Both are cookieless, so your consent setup doesn't change.

steps.title: Rename your goals as events
steps.description: plausible('Signup', { props: { plan: 'pro' } }) becomes op.track('signup', { plan: 'pro' }). Pageview goals need nothing: OpenPanel records every pageview.

steps.title: Identify logged-in users
steps.description: Call op.identify({ profileId }) after login. This is the step Plausible can't do, and it's what retention, cohorts and user profiles need.

steps.title: Rebuild your funnels and dashboards
steps.description: Recreate your Plausible funnels, then add the retention report you couldn't have before.

steps.title: Remove Plausible when you have enough history
steps.description: Compare a few weeks of numbers between the two dashboards, then drop the Plausible script and export anything you want to keep.

sdk_compatibility.notes: Both track named events with a properties object, so goal calls map one to one.

historical_data.notes: OpenPanel can't import Plausible history. Export it from Plausible as CSV before you cancel, and run both tools in parallel during the switch.

faqs.title: Frequently asked questions
faqs.intro: Short answers, including the cases where Plausible wins.

items.question: Is OpenPanel as privacy-friendly as Plausible?
items.answer: For anonymous traffic, yes: neither sets cookies, and both host their cloud in Germany. The difference is that OpenPanel lets you identify logged-in users. If you do, you're processing personal data about those users and should cover it in your privacy policy. If you never call identify, OpenPanel stays anonymous like Plausible.

items.question: Does Plausible have funnels?
items.answer: Yes, on the Business plan. A Plausible funnel has 2 to 8 steps made of pageview or custom event goals, counted per visitor. It can't branch, and you can filter it but not break it down by a property. Funnels aren't included in the self-hosted Community Edition.

items.question: Is OpenPanel cheaper than Plausible?
items.answer: It depends on which Plausible plan you'd need. Against Plausible Business, the plan with funnels, OpenPanel costs less at 10k, 100k and 1M pageviews ($5, $20, $90 against $19, $39, $139) and about the same at 10M ($350 against $339). Against Plausible Starter, OpenPanel costs less at 10k and more from 1M up. Custom events count toward OpenPanel's event total, so check your volume.

items.question: Does either have a free plan?
items.answer: No. Both offer a 30-day trial on their cloud and are free to self-host. OpenPanel's self-hosted version includes every feature; Plausible Community Edition leaves out funnels, user journeys and revenue goals.

items.question: Can I import my Plausible data into OpenPanel?
items.answer: No. OpenPanel imports from Umami, Mixpanel and Amplitude, not Plausible. Run both tools side by side for a few weeks and export your Plausible stats as CSV before you cancel.

items.question: What do I lose by leaving Plausible?
items.answer: Google Analytics import, the sub-1 KB script, and a dashboard so simple nobody needs to learn it. OpenPanel has more reports, which also means more to learn.

items.question: Which is better for a blog or docs site?
items.answer: Plausible, unless you also have a product with logged-in users. For traffic stats alone, its simplicity is the point.
